searchText: I'd love to hear more opinions on whether we should require a builder signature over the `SignedBuilderBid` in addition to the relay signature. https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/23 + https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/4 In the current design, the `BuilderBid` includes the builder pubkey, and the relay could change it to whatever. But even if a builder signature is required, the relay could also just use any keypair and sign it instead of the original builder. 🤔 cc/ <@539495253418180618> <@543900561460822016> I feel like I'd like the additional attribution with a builder signature. https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/23 suggests updating `BuilderBid` + `SignedBuilderbid` like this: 1. Include a builder signature in the `BuilderBid` message that signs over the `header` and `value` data. 2. Include a relay public key along with an outer signature in the `SignedBuilderBid` message. An alternative could be to embed both public keys into `BuilderBid` and have both signatures over the flat structure. I'm checking the `value` field from the bid. I suspect that you are not treating it as a `QUANTITY` but as `DATA`, with the implication of endianness incompatibility when we deserialize from json. https://github.com/flashbots/boost-geth-builder/blob/f65c6da8d9ce9b0421f9911ebcbc43aedf076b7a/builder/backend.go#L251 you see from the screenshot that we get correctly the `BaseFeePerGas` as quantity, but `Value` it definitely too big (it get reversed). <@861612909854588938> can you double-check? In the spec is a uint256, to me sounds a `QUANTITY` <@388610194608750595> getting this on kiln builder: am i postint to correct url 🤔 ?: ```bash Req req-1r registerValidator error invalid json response body at https://builder-relay-kiln.flashbots.net/eth/v1/builder/validators reason: Unexpected end of JSON input FetchError: invalid json response body at https://builder-relay-kiln.flashbots.net/eth/v1/builder/validators reason: Unexpected end of JSON input ``` https://ethereum.github.io/builder-specs/#/Builder/registerValidator has no response body, so you can't json decode got it, but way out api is setup, we need an empty json response still i think easier would be to fix your api setup. otherwise we might want to update the spec too 🤔 iirc, QUANTITY and DATA are json-rpc types, but this is using the CL style: https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/blob/main/types/bellatrix/bid.yaml#L9-L10 -- it's just an integer in a string edit: oh sorry, you didn't mean the API payload but the internal data type well i mean the Bid value as the rewards declared by the builder I think it should be serialized\deserialized the same way as BaseFeePerGas, which is another uin256 QUANTITY that we exchange in the same message since we saw them behaving differently I suspect an issue there, but we are still waiting to grab some http level traces so we can see what is actually exchanged. I don’t see anything against, you should post it as an issue to the builder spec and we can discuss there Ok! Going to doublecheck on or side first and I'll ping you there if it is the case

excerpts.author: metachris_
excerpts.content:
I'd love to hear more opinions on whether we should require a builder signature over the `SignedBuilderBid` in addition to the relay signature. https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/23 + https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/4

In the current design, the `BuilderBid` includes the builder pubkey, and the relay could change it to whatever. But even if a builder signature is required, the relay could also just use any keypair and sign it instead of the original builder. 🤔  cc/ <@539495253418180618> <@543900561460822016>

excerpts.author: metachris_
excerpts.content:
I feel like I'd like the additional attribution with a builder signature.

https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/23 suggests updating `BuilderBid` + `SignedBuilderbid`  like this: 
1. Include a builder signature in the `BuilderBid` message that signs over the `header` and `value` data.
2. Include a relay public key along with an outer signature in the `SignedBuilderBid` message. 

An alternative could be to embed both public keys into `BuilderBid` and have both signatures over the flat structure.
